signals.title: NZD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + RBNZ Hike Pricing
signals.text: NZD leads the G10 currency performance table over the past week with an average gain of +0.580% across 4 pairs, while CHF anchors the laggard slot at -0.720% across 6 pairs, generating an extreme leader-to-laggard bilateral spread of 1.300%. The divergence reflects active policy divergence as the RBNZ faces imminent tightening pressure, supported by local shadow board recommendations and polls favoring a 25bp hike to 3.00%. In contrast, the SNB remains anchored at 0.00% with cash rates at -0.06% SARON, yielding a massive +275bp policy rate advantage favoring NZD. Spot trades at 0.4707, well above the model fair value of 0.4662 (BEER z = +1.85σ rich), reflecting strong bilateral momentum. Technical structure on NZD/USD shows short-term evidence turning against the broader downtrend, reinforcing cross performance. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/CHF, bilateral divergence favored ahead of policy decision. Catalyst: RBNZ Interest Rate Decision 28 Oct at 01:00 UTC. Risk: RBNZ holds rates unexpectedly at 2.75%, unwinding the 1.300% weekly outperformance spread.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew vs Carry
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.53, holding below its daily SMA20 at 157.88, SMA50 at 157.51, and SMA200 at 158.53, preserving a confirmed downtrend structure following a wide-range expansion two sessions ago. Options markets exhibit an acute protective bias with 1-month 25-delta Risk Reversals printing at -2.15, marking an extreme put skew that signals elevated demand for downside hedges. This heavy put pricing contrasts with CFTC Leveraged Funds, where net JPY positioning remains net short -25,598 contracts (pctl 94, z +1.43) despite a WoW short-covering add of +12,222 contracts. A wide SOFR-TONA OIS carry differential of +269bp (Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% policy spread at +275bp) continues to support the underlying pair, while VIX at 18.4 confirms normal cross-asset volatility. The aggressive options skew reflects heightened sensitivity to the upcoming BoJ monetary policy review, where core inflation revisions present event risk to crowded carry positions. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, downside options hedging pressures technical resistance at the 157.88 SMA20. Catalyst: BoJ Interest Rate Decision 30 Oct. Risk: BoJ delivers an entirely dovish hold without dissenters, prompting an immediate squeeze back toward the 158.53 SMA200.

signals.title: USD/NOK — Technical Breakdown vs Retail Extreme
signals.text: USD/NOK trades at 9.322, extending 2.2 ATR below its daily 20-day moving average and sustaining a pronounced downtrend below its SMA20 (9.492), SMA50 (9.409), and SMA200 (9.511). Spot established a fresh 10-day closing low in the prior session, tracking ongoing dollar softness across select G10 crosses. Retail sentiment data retail positioning has pushed to an absolute extreme with 100% long interest, creating severe contrarian unwinding risk as trapped retail longs absorb the trend extension. Real policy rates heavily penalize the pair, with Norges Bank maintaining a restrictive real rate of +1.82% (policy rate 4.5% vs 2.68% inflation expectations) compared to the Fed's real policy rate of +1.61%. While the nominal policy rate spread sits at Fed 4.00% vs Norges Bank 4.50% (50bp carry advantage favoring NOK), USD/NOK trades cheap against BEER fair value at 9.4705 (z = -1.55σ). The persistent spot deterioration despite one-sided retail dip-buying signals institutional flow dominance. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK, trend continuation favored while capped below the 9.409 SMA50. Catalyst: Norges Bank Interest Rate Decision 5 Nov. Risk: Mean-reversion rebound toward fair value at 9.4705 triggered by retail capitulation or crude oil correction.
